question: m12
q: Is electricity inflation running ahead of overall inflation?

transcript.answer:
**Yes. Electricity prices are rising much faster than prices overall.** In the latest monthly CPI, for **August 2026**, electricity prices were up **13.2%** on a year earlier. Overall (all groups) inflation was **4.0%** over the same period, so electricity is running more than three times faster.

**How the gap has moved (annual % change, Australia, original series):**

| Period | Electricity | All groups CPI |
|---|---|---|
| Jun 2025 | −6.3% | 1.9% |
| Oct 2025 | 37.1% | 3.8% |
| Feb 2026 | 37.0% | 3.7% |
| Jun 2026 | 22.4% | 3.8% |
| Jul 2026 | 6.1% | 3.5% |
| Aug 2026 | 13.2% | 4.0% |

**What stands out:**
- **Until mid-2025, electricity was falling.** Annual electricity inflation was negative from January to June 2025 (as low as −13.2% in February). That's most likely because government energy bill rebates were cutting what households paid.
- **Then it jumped.** From July 2025 the annual rate turned sharply positive, peaking at about 37% in October 2025 and February 2026. The likely cause is the rebates shrinking or ending, which pushed up what households actually paid, rather than only higher underlying tariffs.
- **The rate has eased since then, but it's still high.** It dropped to 6.1% in July 2026, probably because it was now being compared with July 2025, when the jump had already started. It then rose back to 13.2% in August.

**Bottom line:** Electricity has been running ahead of headline inflation every month since July 2025. In August 2026 it was ahead by about 9 percentage points (13.2% vs 4.0%). Because rebates shift the timing, the annual electricity figure jumps around a lot from month to month, so it's best read as a trend over several months.
